title: Pilot Starcompass adoption in Orbit
description: Preserve Orbit's complete local rules as an overlay, render a self-contained AGENTS.md from a pinned Starcompass commit, record explicit exceptions, and prove a clean drift check without changing Orbit product behavior.
design: Pilot consumer: Orbit. Compose profiles in ordered form greenfield then terminal-engine. Preserve the complete pre-adoption Orbit AGENTS.md as .agent-protocols.local.md with only its outer heading normalized for embedding. Use an explicit empty schema-1 exceptions file unless semantic review finds a real conflict requiring user approval. The pilot found that generated instructions did not name their editable inputs; the renderer correction and focused check are part of the proof-bearing Starcompass source commit Orbit will pin.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The change explicitly alters no Orbit product contract or runtime behavior. 2. Every pre-adoption Orbit instruction survives byte-for-byte except the normalized outer heading. 3. Orbit records ordered greenfield + terminal-engine profiles, exact Starcompass source commit, protocol IDs, versions, hashes, and zero local exceptions. 4. The structural checker passes using the pinned source checkout. 5. Orbit documentation and repository verification appropriate to an instruction-only change pass. 6. Orbit commits and pushes the scoped adoption without unrelated changes. 7. The Starcompass Bead records exact proof and closes without absorbing unrelated source-repository changes.
notes: The pilot tests the hardest useful first case: a mature local policy with contract, evidence, crate, proof, cross-repository, portability, and exception rules. Remote includes, profile inference, policy deduplication, semantic weakening, and rollout to other consumers remain out of scope.
close_reason: Completed the first Starcompass consumer pilot: Orbit preserves its full local policy, pins proof-bearing Starcompass commit 9cab501, records zero exceptions, passes structural and full repository verification, and is pushed at 5b9efa5.

title: Add optional release promotion and delivery proof profile
description: Contract: a consumer that explicitly selects the Starcompass release profile receives self-contained rules requiring promotion of one exact verified revision through declared ordered channels and proof of the actual packaged or installed artifact in a fresh session. title: Separate unrelated general-purpose Codex skills
description: Decide a separate home for general-purpose skills such as ui, opinion, and readme. Starcompass retains only skills whose sole purpose is applying or auditing canonical protocols. Do not move personal skills until the user selects the destination and migration boundary.

title: Add source-independent consumer check and distribution boundary
description:
## Why

Starcompass is already the sole owner of consumer protocol-import integrity, but its only consumer check requires a clean source checkout containing the canonical protocol and profile catalog. That forces downstream cold CI either to fetch this private repository or to duplicate part of the format locally. Orbit has deliberately rejected both shapes and is waiting for a stable source-independent Starcompass surface.

Operator-visible contract: `starcompass check-consumer --overlay PATH --exceptions PATH --manifest PATH --agents PATH` checks every integrity fact derivable from those four consumer-owned/generated files without a Starcompass checkout, Git repository, protocol/profile catalog, credentials, or network access. The existing source-backed `check` command composes this owner with canonical catalog, exact source-commit, and complete generated-file verification. The consumer check must report its narrower proof honestly: it does not verify canonical protocol prose or manifest protocol digests against source.

A usable downstream boundary also requires one deliberate distribution choice. The current private, `publish = false` package cannot be consumed by cold Orbit CI. Compare and obtain user approval for a published Rust crate/binary package, a public checksum-pinned binary artifact, and an authenticated private artifact. Do not publish, change repository visibility, add hosted CI, or introduce credentials until that choice is explicit.

Impact: P1. This removes duplicate protocol interpretation from Orbit and unblocks the remaining integration condition in `orb-9o6`, which in turn blocks the first Venus consumer bead. Estimated effort: medium. Risk: medium because generated Markdown framing and public distribution can become compatibility and supply-chain surfaces. Confidence: high in the ownership split, medium in the distribution shape until the decision gate is completed.

## Evidence

- `src/lib.rs:120`: manifest, source, protocol-record, exception, and overlay schemas are private typed records and already use strict unknown-field rejection.
- `src/lib.rs:152`: Starcompass already owns SHA-256 calculation.
- `src/lib.rs:475`: exception validation currently depends only on the exception document and selected protocol IDs, so it can be reused by a consumer-only owner.
- `src/lib.rs:639`: generated `AGENTS.md` has a deterministic import record and protocol table.
- `src/lib.rs:708`: the repository-local section is a deterministic final suffix derived from the overlay.
- `src/lib.rs:720`: `validate_manifest` reconstructs the complete import from the source catalog, coupling local validation to source-backed validation.
- `src/lib.rs:757`: `check_import` mixes exception-input parity and generated-file checks with canonical catalog reconstruction.
- `src/lib.rs:904`: `command_check` requires a clean source root and exact source HEAD before checking consumer files.
- `src/lib.rs:1104`: the CLI exposes only the source-backed `check` command.
- `Cargo.toml:6`: the package is explicitly `publish = false`.
- `README.md:108`: incubation currently publishes neither release artifacts nor an installer.
- `docs/DESIGN.md:160`: publication, licensing, releases, and hosted checks remain explicit user decisions.
- `../orbit/README.md:201`: Orbit deliberately does not parse protocol consumer files and names Starcompass as their one owner.
- `../orbit/README.md:205`: Orbit cold CI cannot fetch the private source checker and still needs a stable distribution boundary.
- `../orbit/docs/CRATES.md:15`: Orbit selected no Starcompass dependency until a source-independent, distributable interface exists.
- `orb-9o6`: the active Orbit governance bead records this exact interface and distribution condition before closure.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/lib.rs`: one source-independent validation owner shared by the new command and existing source-backed command.
- `src/lib.rs` command dispatch/help and only the minimum `src/main.rs` boundary adjustment if required.
- `tests/` and focused unit tests: temporary consumer fixtures containing only overlay, exceptions, manifest, and `AGENTS.md`.
- `README.md`, `docs/DESIGN.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and the README LOC scorecard.
- `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` only after the distribution gate selects a package shape that requires metadata changes.
- A durable distribution decision recording artifact identity, versioning, checksums, authentication, licensing, platform coverage, update policy, and replacement cost.
- Starcompass self-adoption refresh through the documented two-revision bootstrap if checker source changes.

Out of scope:
- Canonical protocol or profile changes, new IDs, schema revisions, or semantic-compliance claims.
- Orbit source, CI, governance rules, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/CRATES.md`, or Beads conventions; `orb-9o6` owns downstream integration.
- Parsing or claiming verification of canonical protocol prose without the pinned source catalog.
- Vendoring, copying logic, Git submodules, path dependencies, or an Orbit-specific adapter.
- Repository visibility changes, public publication, hosted CI, secrets, installer frameworks, signing services, or release automation without a separate explicit user decision.
- Remote transport, runtime networking, automatic consumer mutation, or compatibility aliases beyond `check-consumer`.

## Implementation Notes

1. Begin after `ap-85h` closes. Re-read the simplified checker and update this evidence if symbols or boundaries moved materially.
2. State and test the consumer-only invariant set before refactoring:
   - manifest schema is 1; source repository is non-empty; source commit is a lowercase 40-character Git SHA;
   - profile names are non-empty and unique while preserving order;
   - protocol records have unique valid IDs, positive versions, and lowercase 64-character SHA-256 values while preserving order;
   - overlay bytes hash exactly to the manifest overlay digest;
   - exception input is strict schema-1 JSON, validates against manifest protocol IDs, and equals the manifest exception list exactly;
   - the generated `AGENTS.md` source, commit, profiles, manifest schema marker, and protocol import table equal the manifest exactly;
   - the complete final `## Repository-local rules` suffix equals the deterministic rendering of the overlay exactly.
3. Add one internal consumer-validation owner. Keep format parsing narrow and explicit. Return deterministic actionable failures that name the mismatched surface. Do not reconstruct the canonical catalog or accept a source root.
4. Add the `check-consumer` CLI with the same four path arguments as `check`. Make `check` call the consumer validator first, then perform exact source HEAD, catalog/profile/protocol, canonical prose, and full rendered-file validation. Delete duplicated validation created by the split.
5. Use one strong temporary-directory contract test proving success with only four consumer files and no `.git`, `protocols/`, or `profiles/`. Mutate each locally knowable relationship in turn and assert failure. Retain a source-backed composition test proving canonical body/catalog drift still fails only under `check`.
6. Run a distribution gate before changing package/release metadata. At minimum compare:
   - a crates.io package exposing the CLI and, only if downstream code needs it, a small library API;
   - a publicly downloadable, versioned binary with published SHA-256 per supported target;
   - an authenticated private package or release with explicit GitHub Actions secret and fork behavior;
   - no distribution yet.
   Record public-source implications, package-name availability, licensing, MSRV, compile/download cost, target coverage, checksum/signing model, revocation/yank behavior, credentials, maintenance, and exit cost. Preserve the rejected vendoring, submodule, copied-parser, and private Git dependency shapes.
7. Stop for explicit user approval of the selected distribution and any licensing, publication, repository visibility, credential, target-support, or hosted-automation consequence. After approval, implement only the smallest selected artifact boundary and prove its immutable identity from a clean environment without relying on a Starcompass checkout.
8. Update current-state documentation and LOC evidence. If checker source changes, commit and verify it under the existing pin, then refresh self-adoption from that exact clean revision in the required follow-up revision.

No new parser, CLI, error, test, hashing, HTTP, release, or signing crate is expected. Any proposed dependency requires a fresh crate gate with standard-library and multiple credible alternatives before manifest edits.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked check_consumer` should exit 0 and prove a valid four-file fixture needs no source root while representative manifest, overlay, exception, import-table, and local-suffix drift each fail.
- `cargo test --locked` should exit 0 and retain source-backed render/check, deterministic bytes, exception, version-history, and process behavior.
- `cargo run --locked --quiet -- check-consumer --overlay FIXTURE/.agent-protocols.local.md --exceptions FIXTURE/.agent-protocols.exceptions.json --manifest FIXTURE/.agent-protocols.json --agents FIXTURE/AGENTS.md` should exit 0 outside any Starcompass checkout and report only the consumer-local proof.
- The corresponding source-backed `check` should still reject a checkout whose HEAD or canonical catalog does not match the manifest.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, and `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` should exit 0.
- Both protocol skill validators named in `AGENTS.md` should exit 0.
- The exact-pinned Starcompass self-import check from `README.md` should exit 0 after the two-revision refresh.
- A clean-environment distribution proof should retrieve or build the approved exact artifact, verify its immutable version/checksum, and run the four-file fixture without source-repository access. Hosted CI is not required or authorized by this bead.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0, and README LOC totals should equal the changed tracked surfaces.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if `ap-85h` changes the cited checker architecture enough that this ownership split is no longer the smallest complete shape.
- Stop if consumer-only verification would need canonical protocol prose or a source catalog; keep that proof in source-backed `check`.
- Stop before any publication, licensing, visibility, credentials, target-support, hosted-CI, or compatibility decision not explicitly approved by the user.
- Stop if implementation requires editing Orbit or another consumer.
- Stop if a new dependency appears necessary before completing and recording a crate gate.
- Stop if verification fails twice for the same reason after a reasonable fix attempt.

## Maintenance Notes

- One owner is the review focus: source-independent format interpretation belongs in Starcompass; consumers call it and retain only repository-local governance.
- `check-consumer` is intentionally a narrower proof than `check`. Documentation and success text must not imply canonical prose or source-pin verification.
- Prefer a binary-only downstream boundary unless a concrete consumer needs an in-process Rust API; a public library API creates a larger compatibility promise.
- The current preferred distribution candidates are a published Rust package or a public checksum-pinned binary. Neither is preapproved by this bead.
- Review malformed Markdown handling, duplicate headings/tables, delimiter ambiguity, path-independent diagnostics, and exact byte behavior at the trust boundary.
- Revisit the distribution choice when supported targets, MSRV, schema version, authentication model, or release ownership changes.

title: Fresh-eyes audit and isomorphic simplification of the Rust checker
description: Contract: review the Rust checker migration from scratch, fix confirmed correctness, compatibility, security, documentation, or verification defects, and remove accidental complexity only where observable Starcompass behavior remains equivalent. Preserve accepted commands and arguments, exit behavior, deterministic JSON and AGENTS.md bytes, ordering, schemas, hashes, exact-pin and source-cleanliness checks, atomic replacement, validation boundaries, generated-file ownership, and the two-revision self-adoption bootstrap. Any intentional hardening of invalid input must be named separately from isomorphic cleanup. Do not add a dependency, protocol, profile, hosted CI, packaging surface, or unrelated feature. Proof must include a pre-edit baseline, explicit candidate scoring and isomorphism card, focused regression tests for confirmed bugs, byte/output comparison, full Rust and skill checks, updated LOC/evidence, a checker source commit, and a follow-up exact-pinned self-adoption commit if checker source changes.
design: Fresh-eyes findings and candidate scoring (2026-08-04). BUG F1: serde Option<String> accepts an explicit JSON null for review_condition, while the Python owner required every present exception field to be a non-empty string. BUG F2: valid_date accepts year 0000, while Python date.fromisoformat rejected it. BUG F3: atomic-write-file defaults preserve existing Unix ownership and mode and create new files as 0666 masked by umask; a measured new render produced 0664, while the Python writer created a fresh file and fchmoded it to 0644. SECURITY F4: an option-like --base value is concatenated into git show without rejecting a leading dash. Fix F1-F4 with focused tests; F1/F2 restore invalid-input compatibility, F3 restores Unix file side effects while retaining cross-platform atomic replacement, and F4 intentionally tightens invalid input. Simplification S1: validate_manifest returns a Manifest its sole caller discards; return only rendered text (about 2 LOC and one unnecessary value removed, confidence 100%, strong tests, negligible risk). S2: Protocol::import_record has one call site; inline it (about 4 LOC removed, confidence 100%, strong render tests). S3: commit grammar is duplicated; extract one predicate and reuse it for manifest/source validation and leading-dash revision rejection (small LOC reduction plus one validation owner, confidence 95%, low risk). S4: json_format_matches_the_compatibility_surface repeats pretty-print/newline behavior already proved by the exact current index byte assertion; delete it (about 10 test LOC and one weak test removed, confidence 95%). Reject a shared directory-listing helper because it saves too little while obscuring protocol/profile diagnostics. Reject a CLI framework or schema rewrite because it adds dependency or behavior risk. Isomorphism card: accepted valid commands, status/success text, manifest and AGENTS bytes, hashes, profile/protocol order, JSON field order/schema, source pin, drift detection, writes, and atomic all-old/all-new semantics remain identical; errors remain actionable, with only null review conditions, year zero, and option-like revisions newly/re-again rejected. No logs, metrics, network, auth, async, timers, retries, UI, or lifecycle hooks exist. Unix output replacement returns to fresh-owner mode 0644; non-Unix atomic behavior remains crate-owned. Baseline at a65b2b3: 11 tests, fmt/check/clippy/validate/version and both skill validators pass; representative greenfield plus terminal-engine hashes are manifest 79878e5ed4808d6f6aaaf98b51671fd1ef7c77e6e8f7df66e840d9f43629e741 and AGENTS 929be6f83ee06ceef435ed8697bbcf6862a4eeac20d1eb14ddca5a6be3951cd8, with measured new-file mode 0664. Verification after: red-then-green focused tests, normalized byte comparison with the baseline, full repository checks, exact-pinned self-check, LOC metrics, then the two-revision self-adoption refresh.
notes: Fresh-eyes F5 discovered by portability proof before source commit: cargo +1.87.0 check fails at four let-chain expressions even though Cargo.toml declares Rust 1.85. All resolved dependencies declare rust-version at or below 1.85, but the local syntax raised the effective floor. Replace only those chains with pre-1.88 stable Option or nested control flow; valid behavior is identical. Verify on the oldest locally installed toolchain, 1.87.0, and record that exact 1.85 was not installed rather than overstating proof.

title: Ship the v1 canonical protocol registry and drift checker
description: Contract: publish stable individually versioned protocol sources, four composable profiles (greenfield, fork, orchestrator, terminal-engine), a self-contained AGENTS.md renderer whose import record includes source commit and approved exceptions, structural drift detection, focused tests, and protocol-only Codex skills. Keep runtime dependencies at zero beyond Python 3 standard library. Rejected for v1: remote includes, semantic-compliance claims, a YAML dependency, hosted CI, and automatic edits to consumer repositories.
design: Canonical Markdown files own prose and metadata; a generated JSON index owns hashes; JSON profiles compose by ordered union. One Python 3 standard-library tool owns indexing, version-history enforcement, deterministic rendering, and structural drift checks. Consumer-local overlay and exception inputs remain separate from generated manifest and AGENTS.md. The source repo bootstraps its own hand-authored AGENTS.md because a self-pin would be recursive.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Exactly four requested profiles validate and can compose without duplicate protocol IDs. 2. Every imported protocol records ID, version, digest, source repository, and exact commit in the manifest and rendered AGENTS.md. 3. Local exceptions record protocol, scope, reason, approver, and date and are visible in AGENTS.md. 4. Drift in protocol sources, index, profile, overlay, exception input, manifest, generated AGENTS.md, or source checkout fails. 5. Protocol IDs cannot disappear and changed protocol files require higher versions. 6. Unit tests and both skill validators pass. 7. A clean committed checkout completes a public CLI render/check round trip.
notes: Dependency gate: selected Python 3 standard library over Rust (consumer toolchain/build burden), POSIX shell (fragile JSON/Unicode/error handling), and YAML/TOML parsers (new dependency or custom dialect). Exit cost is low because input/output schemas are plain Markdown and JSON. Hosted CI, remote includes, semantic compliance claims, and consumer mutations remain out of v1. Proof at 1553f1486e91408c404dab6a232a87563cd8e453: catalog validation passed for 18 protocols and four profiles; nine unit tests passed; Ruff formatting and lint passed; both skills passed quick_validate; version-check against HEAD passed; a clean-checkout public CLI round trip rendered and checked composed greenfield + terminal-engine output at mode 0644.
close_reason: Completed the v1 catalog, composable profiles, pinned self-contained renderer, history and drift gates, tests, documentation, and protocol-only skills; public CLI round trip passed at the recorded bootstrap SHA.

title: Replace the Python protocol checker with Rust
description: Contract: the Starcompass executable becomes the sole checker/renderer owner and preserves the accepted command names, arguments, exit codes, deterministic JSON and AGENTS.md bytes, profile ordering, validation boundaries, exact-pin checks, atomic output intent, and actionable diagnostics of scripts/protocols.py for supported inputs. Python may exist only as a temporary comparison oracle and must be deleted before closure together with Python tests and command references. Protocol files, profiles, IDs, versions, consumer filenames, schemas, manifest provenance, and skills remain compatible. The rewrite must add no hosted CI or new product feature. Before code shape: compare the Rust standard library and multiple credible crates for JSON, SHA-256, CLI parsing, temporary/atomic files, errors, and tests; pin exact winners and record dependency graph, licensing, portability, owned LOC, and exit cost. Proof: capture Python baselines; add Rust parity/contract tests; byte-compare representative render output; run format, check, test, clippy with denied warnings, skill validation, exact-pinned self-check, diff check, and LOC scorecard. Commit the Rust source replacement first, then render and commit Starcompass self-adoption from that exact clean source revision.
design: Crate gate (2026-08-04, rustc/cargo 1.96.0, x86_64 Linux): select exact serde 1.0.229 with derive plus serde_json 1.0.151 for typed schema ownership and deterministic JSON; reject a handwritten JSON parser as duplicated security-sensitive format ownership, json 0.12.4 as weaker typed integration, and simd-json because performance is irrelevant. Select exact sha2 0.11.0 with default features disabled; reject owned SHA-256, external sha256sum, ring 0.17.14, and system crypto because the pure-Rust crate narrowly owns the required portable algorithm. Select exact atomic-write-file 0.3.0; reject std-only temp-plus-rename because Windows overwrite semantics would diverge, tempfile because it owns a broader lifecycle rather than atomic replacement, and direct platform bindings because they create local portability code. Select std::env for the fixed CLI over clap 4.6.5, lexopt 0.3.2, and pico-args 0.5.0; select an owned small error type over anyhow 1.0.104 and thiserror 2.0.19; select std test/process/temp-directory helpers over assert_cmd, predicates, snapbox, and tempfile. Measured candidate graph: four direct crates, 31 registry packages across all target/build metadata, 4.2 MiB unoptimized empty candidate binary; licenses are BSD-3-Clause, MIT, Apache-2.0, Unicode-3.0, Unlicense, and platform-only approved combinations, with no GPL-only package. Serde/JSON and SHA calls remain localized; atomic replacement sits behind one function, giving low exit cost. No CLI/error/test framework dependency. Rust 1.85 and edition 2024 are the minimum candidate baseline. Primary references: serde.rs and serde-rs/json; RustCrypto sha2; andreacorbellini/rust-atomic-write-file; crates.io metadata and exact crate sources.
acceptance_criteria: Isomorphism card: accepted supported inputs retain byte-identical manifest and AGENTS.md rendering, field and profile order, hashes, schemas, source provenance, success text, exit 0/1, and atomic all-or-old output intent. Validation retains permanent IDs, required version bumps, strict source cleanliness, profile composition, explicit exceptions, authoring-file drift, manifest drift, and generated-file drift. No network, async, telemetry, permissions, or lifecycle behavior is added. Exact argparse help prose, Python exception wording, and undocumented invalid JSON/date forms are not stable contracts; Rust must keep commands discoverable and diagnostics actionable. Python baseline at 8fb6803f2ec4036ab499c117b897da469fd9e77e: manifest SHA-256 efa52cb56cc429054fcdf5f66c4cdb29d7ce95747c4fc53a5a3559c2c055a1a0, rendered AGENTS SHA-256 e757548ab7072ea4a6abd105cc9806e69853b505ce907e025e90d853d613f8c8, 10 tests green. Verification after: temporary byte-parity oracle, durable Rust contract tests, cargo fmt/check/test/clippy -D warnings, exact-pinned self-check, both skill validators, diff check, and updated dependency/LOC evidence. Residual risk is limited to obscure invalid-input diagnostic wording and platform behavior not locally run; atomic-write-file owns the cross-platform replacement boundary.
notes: Python-to-Rust parity proof completed before deleting the oracle. At 8fb6803f2ec4036ab499c117b897da469fd9e77e, greenfield plus terminal-engine rendering matched Python byte-for-byte: manifest efa52cb56cc429054fcdf5f66c4cdb29d7ce95747c4fc53a5a3559c2c055a1a0 and AGENTS e757548ab7072ea4a6abd105cc9806e69853b505ce907e025e90d853d613f8c8. The exception fixture covering JSON field order, pipe and newline escaping, approval rendering, and review conditions also matched: manifest 72d888af971d2bbe18a1439bb90d0e1f527cd9a0628e1a060a6a42c5bba8509a and AGENTS ea81d3975da2ffbc682b77df5b251599ef7e0c8f4a4ecefc7636b06e4a3b9f4e. The temporary oracle hash test was removed after proof; 11 durable Rust tests cover deterministic rendering, current index bytes, composition, exceptions, version history, drift, validation, and real process behavior. Final source revision: 30b745bfc619183296957ac03af42e365caf6c21. The compatibility audit restored render without an exceptions argument. Production checker plus package manifest is 1,141 LOC versus the former 620; tests are 377 versus 252. This is a deliberate typed and portable trade, with no CLI, error, test, async, or runtime framework. The four direct exact dependencies resolve to 31 registry packages across all target and build metadata; the optimized Linux binary is 1002 KiB. Final proof passed: cargo fmt, check, 11 tests, clippy with denied warnings, release build, validate, version-check, render both with and without exceptions, exact-pinned self-check, both skill validators, and git diff check. Starcompass self-adoption was rendered from the clean source revision and pins that exact revision.
close_reason: Rust checker is the sole implementation; compatibility, self-adoption, documentation, and verification are complete.

title: Self-adopt the greenfield Starcompass profile
description: Contract: an agent opening Starcompass reads one self-contained generated AGENTS.md whose canonical greenfield rules are pinned to exact source revision db190113958f64e936bf9441fe3fa905c24a632d, while every pre-adoption repository rule survives verbatim in the local overlay and no exception is invented. The normal consumer manifest, overlay, exception input, renderer, and checker remain the owners; do not add a self-hosting profile, special checker mode, dependency, or same-commit pin.
